title: Big Federal Aid for Austin's Utilities, Parking, Parks
summary:
*   **Secured Major Federal Funding:** Approved a $129,500 federal Public Works Administration (PWA) loan and grant to significantly upgrade the city's waterworks and electric light systems, including new pumps, a turbo-generator, and a 6-million-gallon settling basin.
*   **Guadalupe Street Parking Debate:** Initiated action on a request from local merchants to allow parallel parking on the east side of Guadalupe Street (21st-24th) to ease congestion, despite protests from University officials who were granted a future hearing.
*   **Community Projects Under Review:** Considered citizen petitions advocating for the city to purchase the Westenfield Swimming Pool and Park, and a request for financial assistance for the construction of a Texas Centennial museum on the University campus.

REGULAR MEETING OF THE CITY COUNCIL:
Austin, Texas, June 22, 1934.
Roll call showed
The meeting was called to order, with Mayor Tom Miller presiding. the following members
present: Councilmen C. F. Alford, C. M. Bartholomew, Simon Gillis, Mayor Tom Miller, and
Councilman Oswald G. Wolf, 5; absent, none.
Upon motion of Councilman Alford, the regular order of business was suspended and
committees were heard as follows: A committee of merchants on the west side of Guadalupe
Street from 21st to 24th Streets: asked that parking be allowed on the east side of said
street in order to relieve the crowded condition on the west side, which is detrimental to
their business. 476 Councilman Gillis moved that the City Attorney be instructed to
prepare an ordinance establishing parallel parking on the east side of Guadalupe Street
from 21st to 24th Streets, reserving spaces on each side of the entrances to the Campus as
safety zones, and repealing all ordinances in conflict therewith.
The motion was adopted by the following vote: Ayes, Councilmen Alford, Bartholomew,
Gillis, Mayor Miller, and Councilman Wolf, 5; naye, none.
Dr. J. W. Calhoun's protest, on behalf of the University officials, against the above
action was heard and the Council agreed to give the University Board of Regents a hearing
on the matter at such time as they may designate.
A committee of journeymen plumbers asked for the appointment of an assistant plumbing
inspector to lighten the work of the plumbing inspector. The matter was referred to the
City Manager to determine the necessity for same and to make his recommendations to the
Couno11.
R. T. Miller, et al., submitted petitions, signed by a large number of residents and
taxpayers, asking that the City take immediate steps to purchase the Westenfield Swimming
Pool and Park in order that they may not be deprived further of the use of same. After
considerable discussion, the matter was taken under advisement.
Garland Adair, representing the American Legion Texas Centennial Committee, asked for
financial assistance from the City in putting on their coin sales campaign, the proceeds
of which to be used in the construction of a museum on the University Campus as a part of
the Texas Centennial program, the City to be reimbursed for such expenditure. The matter
was taken under advisement.
